reason: Conversation 1 followed the sensible first step of asking which switch trips and whether there was any smell, kept the diagnosis honestly open between RCD/earth-leakage and overload/connection causes, and correctly escalated to an NICEIC/NAPIT electrician, then tightened its safety advice (minimise use, isolate at the cooker switch if the smell recurs, electrician soon) once the electrical smell emerged. Conversation 2 went straight to a hard 'stop using' with no questions, told the homeowner to leave a hardwired hob 'unplugged', and asserted an insulation fault in a coil or power module as the most likely cause, which overstates certainty given the genuinely uncertain hidden truth. Neither recommended parts, which is correct, but Conversation 1 delivered a far more useful, accurate and proportionate service while still landing on the right escalation.
